data.name: Disposable Heroes
data.detailed_description:
Meet the disposable heroes... A rag-tag band of nobodies who - quite by accident - represent the kingdom's last hope.
With the royal army slain it is they who must venture across the land on a quest to bring back the head of the king's son so that the light might return. If they had a brain cell between them they might actually be dangerous. -The game will have a 2 player co-op system.
(Play alone or let a friend join the game to fight side by side with you on your quest.)

ONCE UPON A TIME, IN A LAND FORGOTTEN BY MANY, LIVED A KING AND HIS WIFE, HAPPILY MARRIED AND LOVED BY THEIR SUBJECTS.

ON ONE DAY THE NEWSBOY SHOUTED ‘LONG LIVE THE KING AND HIS SON! LONG LIVE THE KING AND HIS SON!’

BUT THE DAY THE NEWBORN SAW THE LIGHT FOR THE FIRST TIME, SOMETHING TERRIBLE HAPPENED… THE SUN, WHICH HAD SHONE SO BRIGHTLY, DISAPPEARED WHEN THE BOY WAS BORN. CITIZENS WERE SHOCKED, THE KING AND HIS WIFE PARALYZED.

THE CHILD WAS SO HIDEOUS, SO UGLY AND DESPICABLE THAT NOT EVEN HIS OWN FATHER COULD BEAR TO LOOK AT HIM!

THE TOWNSFOLK DEMANDED THAT THE KING WOULD SACRIFICE HIS SON TO MAKE THE SUN COME BACK AND FILL THE LAND WITH HAPPINESS AGAIN…

TWO YEARS OF DARKNESS, HUNGER AND SICKNESS PASSED WHEN THE KING MADE A DECISION – HE WOULD SACRIFICE HIS ONLY SON TO SAVE THE KINGDOM FROM THIS CURSE.

AFTER HEARING HIS FATHER’S THROUGH THE THIN WALLS OF THE CASTLE, THE CHILD ESCAPED THROUGH A SECRET PASSAGE AND FLED INTO THE FOREST WHERE HE WOULD LIVE THE REST OF HIS LIFE…

THE KING SENT HIS BEST MEN INTO THE DARK LANDS, BUT NONE OF HIS SOLDIERS RETURNED. THE EVIL IN THE KINGDOM GREW STRONGER, AND WITHOUT THE LIGHT OF THE SUN THE LAND WOULD BE DOOMED FOREVER.

SINCE THERE WERE NO SOLDIERS LEFT, THE KING GATHERED A GROUP OF FOUR STRONG VILLAGERS TO KILL THE LAD AND BRING BACK HIS HEAD…

…UNFORTUNATELY THESE WERE THE ONLY FOUR LEFT…

+ More than 140 levels
+ Lots of weapons (Swords/magic wands/Flying orbs)
+ Magical potions
+ 10 Achievements
+ Bags of gold
+ Random spawning of useless stuff
+ 4 different hero characters
+ More than 90 different enemies
+ Secret passages and hidden rooms
+ Magical flying goats
+ Save your progress
+ Animated cutscene
+ Heroic music
+ Random bonus levels
+ Co-op gameplay
+ Special guests Appearances like Robin Hood
+ Voice acting and narration
+ Wacky humor
+ Lots of traps like Poison arrows and cutting lasers
+ bosses that are too big to fit inside the screen

Player 1
Movement : W/A/S/D
Action Primary: C
Action Secondary: V
Use Objects: 1/2/3/4/5

Player 2
Movement : Arrows
Action Primary: N
Action Secondary: M
Use Objects: 6/7/8/9/0

This game only supports XBOX 360 controllers

This game comes with steam trading cards and achievements

reviews.review:
Disposable Heroes takes the familiar fantasy story of a kingdom in crisis and turns it into an intentionally ridiculous action adventure. Instead of assembling legendary knights destined to save the realm, the game follows four unlikely villagers who are essentially the kingdom's last available option. Developed by Stake deep interactive and published by Evilized productions, it embraces the rough, playful character of a small indie project, combining straightforward combat, exploration, traps, secrets, cooperative play, and an abundance of absurd humor.

The story establishes that unusual personality immediately. A prince is born just as the sun mysteriously disappears, leaving the kingdom trapped in darkness. As hunger, illness, and desperation spread, the population begins blaming the royal child for its suffering. The king eventually decides that sacrificing his own son may restore the sun, but the prince escapes before the plan can be completed. Soldiers sent to retrieve him fail to return, leaving four ordinary and thoroughly expendable adventurers to continue the hunt. It is deliberately twisted fantasy storytelling, treating what could have been a grim fairy tale with exaggerated comedy rather than seriousness.

The adventure is surprisingly substantial in terms of raw content. There are more than 140 levels to work through, alongside over 90 varieties of enemies, large bosses, hidden locations, secret passages, random bonus stages, environmental hazards, and collectible objects. Levels regularly introduce traps such as poison arrows and lasers, while the creatures and situations encountered along the journey become increasingly strange. Exploration therefore has some value beyond simply finding the exit. Searching suspicious corners can reveal hidden areas or useful items, while the unpredictable bonus stages help break up the normal progression.

Combat is accessible rather than technically demanding. The four heroes can make use of swords, magical wands, potions, flying orbs, and various other objects encountered throughout the journey. The mechanics do not offer the complexity of a dedicated action RPG, but that simplicity works reasonably well with the game's arcade-like pacing. Encounters are primarily about surviving enemies and hazards while moving forward, rather than mastering elaborate skill combinations or developing highly specialized character builds. Some players may find this structure repetitive after extended sessions, particularly because the huge number of levels exceeds the variety of the underlying combat system.

A major advantage is the option to bring another player along. Two-player cooperative support complements the chaotic nature of the adventure extremely well. Having two unlikely heroes battling monsters and stumbling through dangerous environments makes many of the game's ridiculous situations more entertaining. The Steam release also supports Remote Play Together, allowing its local cooperative design to be used remotely. Solo play remains perfectly viable, but multiplayer is arguably where the game's deliberately messy and humorous personality becomes most enjoyable.

Its presentation follows the same philosophy. Animated sequences, narration, voice acting, fantasy music, exaggerated creatures, strange guest appearances, and concepts such as magical flying goats ensure that the game rarely behaves like a conventional heroic fantasy. There is a homemade quality to much of the presentation that can be charming when approached with the right expectations. The comedy is frequently silly and sometimes deliberately crude, meaning players looking for sophisticated storytelling probably will not find much satisfaction here. The game is more interested in creating unexpected situations and visual jokes than developing an emotionally serious narrative.

Age is one of its more noticeable weaknesses. Originally released in 2015, its controls, interface choices, visual presentation, and general mechanical simplicity can feel dated compared with newer indie action games. Controller information was designed around hardware common to its release period, and some aspects lack the refinement expected from modern releases. The large stage count also means that repetition inevitably appears. Players motivated by secrets, unusual enemies, and constant changes of scenery are more likely to remain interested than those primarily seeking deep combat.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially categorized as Playable rather than fully Verified. Performance with the default graphics configuration is considered suitable, and the game can run successfully on SteamOS. However, handheld players should expect compromises. Some functionality is not fully accessible through the default controller configuration, touchscreen interaction or a community controller layout may occasionally be useful, and text entry can require manually opening the virtual keyboard. Some interface text may also appear small, while certain prompts can display keyboard, mouse, or non-Steam Deck controller icons. It is therefore functional on the Deck, but the experience is less seamless than a fully optimized handheld release.

Disposable Heroes ultimately succeeds more through personality and quantity than refinement. Its huge collection of stages, numerous enemy types, hidden areas, cooperative support, bizarre equipment, traps, bosses, and constant nonsense create an adventure that feels enthusiastically unconventional. The basic combat and dated presentation prevent it from becoming an outstanding action game, but there is something appealing about how confidently it commits to being strange. For players who enjoy obscure indie titles, local cooperative adventures, and fantasy games that refuse to take themselves seriously, there is enough here to make this collection of expendable heroes worth sending into danger.

Rating: 6/10
